# `delivery-schedule` commands

## `delivery-schedule create`

Save a recurring batch: kind and selection as delivery batch takes them (statements take a period word), a frequency from start_date (a month-end start stays at month end), optional stop_date or remaining_runs. Each slot runs once on the host; after downtime only the latest missed slot runs, within catch_up_days (7). mode send is a draft until a person makes it live. Missing details are refused, never guessed. Example: {"name": "Month-end statements", "kind": "statement", "period": "month-to-date", "balance_over": "0", "frequency": "monthly", "start_date": "2026-10-31", "mode": "send"}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | customer |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member, customer-work: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/delivery-schedule.create` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow delivery-schedule create --name "Month-end statements" --kind statement --period month-to-date --balance-over 0 --frequency monthly --start-date 2026-11-30 --mode send --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Statements each month end" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```

## `delivery-schedule live`

Make a send schedule live: its runs then release with your go and pause if you lose it. One check first: run it with dry_run, show the person the check (selection, cadence, first run, who it would reach today), then run it with the check's fingerprint as confirm. A person's act.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | customer |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member, customer-work: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/delivery-schedule.live` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow delivery-schedule live "Month-end statements" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --dry-run --json`

### MCP

```

## `delivery-schedule pause`

Stop a schedule: nothing runs until it is resumed.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

## `delivery-schedule resume`

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

## `delivery-schedule update`

Change a schedule. A change to what or when it sends returns a live one to draft, unless a person passes the changed schedule's check fingerprint as confirm (dry_run shows it).

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | customer |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member, customer-work: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/delivery-schedule.update` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow delivery-schedule update "Month-end statements" --combine --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "One email each" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "delivery-schedule update", "input": {"schedule": "Month-end statements", "combine": true}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `queued` | `--queued` | boolean \| null | no | yes | null | Every to-be-emailed document (of kind). |
| `unsent` | `--unsent` | boolean \| null | no | yes | null | Documents of kind with no live or sent message. |
| `ready` | `--ready` | boolean \| null | no | yes | null | kind notice: every ready overdue notice. |
| `period` | `--period` | literal["previous-month", "month-to-date", "since-last-run"] \| null | no | yes | null | Statements: previous-month, month-to-date (to the run's day) or since-last-run (from the day after the last run's period; the first run takes the previous month). |
| `customer` | `--customer` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Only this customer and its jobs. |
| `customer_type` | `--customer-type` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Only customers of this type. |
| `balance_over` | `--balance-over` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Statements: a balance over this. |
| `method` | `--method` | literal["email"] \| null | no | yes | null | Statements: only customers whose method is email. |
| `combine` | `--combine` | boolean \| null | no | yes | null | One message per customer with all its documents. |
| `template` | `--template` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Template; default the kind's default. |
| `frequency` | `--frequency` | literal["daily", "weekly", "every_other_week", "every_four_weeks", "twice_a_month", "monthly", "every_other_month", "quarterly", "twice_a_year", "annually"] \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `start_date` | `--start-date` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The first slot. A month-end start stays at month end. |
| `stop_date` | `--stop-date` | string \| null | no | yes | null | No slot after this day. |
| `remaining_runs` | `--remaining-runs` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | Stop after this many runs. |
| `mode` | `--mode` | literal["draft", "send"] \| null | no | yes | null | draft: each run leaves drafts. send: each run releases them; they leave only once a person has made the schedule live (delivery-schedule live), and until then wait for a go. |
| `catch_up_days` | `--catch-up-days` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | After the host was off, the latest missed slot runs only if no older than this (default 7). |
| `schedule` | `SCHEDULE` | string | yes | no | — | Schedule name or id.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1004 |
| `name` | `--name` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `kind` | `--kind` | literal["invoice", "sales-receipt", "estimate", "statement", "notice"] \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `no_end` | `--no-end` | boolean | no | no | false | Clear stop_date and remaining_runs. |
| `confirm` | `--confirm` | string \| null | no | yes | null | A live schedule stays live through a change only when a person passes the fingerprint of the check the dry run shows for the changed schedule; otherwise the change returns it to draft. |
| `expected_version` | `--expected-version` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | — |

### Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_COMPANY_AMBIGUOUS` | More than one company matches; use the id or Organization/Company. |
| `E_COMPANY_NOT_FOUND` | No such company. |
| `E_CONFIG_INVALID` | The configuration file could not be read. |
| `E_CONTEXT_IN_INPUT` | Input contains a context field. |
| `E_DB_BUSY` | Another Bookflow command is running on this data root. |
| `E_DIRECTIVE_INACTIVE` | That directive has been deactivated. |
| `E_DIRECTIVE_NOT_FOUND` | No such directive. |
| `E_FEATURE_DISABLED` | This feature is not enabled for the company. |
| `E_FS_UNKNOWN` | The filesystem type of the path could not be determined. |
| `E_GUARD_REFUSED` | Bookflow's own safety check in the database refused this write, so nothing was saved. This is a Bookflow bug, not a problem with your input or your disk: please report it with this error's details and request id. |
| `E_IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH` | That idempotency key was used for a different command or input. |
| `E_INTERNAL` | Internal failure. |
| `E_IO` | A filesystem operation failed. |
| `E_MIGRATION_FAILED` | A schema migration failed; the database was backed up first and is unchanged. |
| `E_NETWORK_SHARE` | The path is on a network filesystem, which Bookflow refuses to use. |
| `E_NOT_INITIALIZED` | The data root is not initialized; run `bookflow init`. |
| `E_NO_ACTOR` | This login is not mapped to a Bookflow user. |
| `E_ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND` | No such organization. |
| `E_PARTIAL_WRITE` | The authoritative write committed, but a secondary update remains incomplete. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The acting user may not run this command here. |
| `E_REASON_REQUIRED` | This write needs a reason: a short phrase naming what triggered it (--reason on the CLI, a top-level reason on MCP, the X-Bookflow-Reason header on HTTP). |
| `E_RECORD_NOT_FOUND` | No such record. |
| `E_SCHEMA_BEHIND` | The database schema is behind this version of Bookflow; run `bookflow upgrade`. |
| `E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN` | The database schema revision is not known to this version of Bookflow; upgrade Bookflow. |
| `E_UNAUTHENTICATED` | No valid credential: log in, or send a bearer token. |
| `E_USAGE` | Invalid command syntax. |
| `E_VALIDATION` | Invalid input. |
| `E_VERSION_CONFLICT` | The record changed since the version you read. |
| `E_WORK_DEPENDENCY` | The accepted or linked work prevents this change; inspect the related document. |
